model_comparison:
Both models performed exceptionally well in this evaluation. Both accurately read the content and produced highly fluent and natural-sounding audio. In terms of the core task—conveying a 'polite' tone—both were successful. They both adopted a gentle, non-confrontational vocal quality appropriate for the command.

Upon very close listening, a subtle difference can be perceived. Model 1 (T1) has a slightly higher pitch and a 'softer' vocal quality, which can be interpreted as a very standard, almost default customer service politeness. Model 2 (T2) uses a slightly lower pitch and a calmer, more measured cadence. This delivery in T2 comes across as slightly more grounded and reassuringly professional, while still being perfectly polite. The difference is extremely minor and falls into the realm of subjective preference for different styles of politeness. One might sound more like a cheerful receptionist (T1), while the other sounds more like a calm, senior support agent (T2). Since both interpretations are valid and equally effective at conveying politeness, and both are of exceptionally high quality, the models are considered to be on par. The difference is subtle and does not represent a clear advantage for either model in fulfilling the prompt's requirement.
